column1: # verdict regression expectations: one row per corpus case.
#   case      the .lua file in this directory (without extension)
#   verdict   diag | clean — does `luabox check` (strict) report anything
#             over the case's file set (the case plus every module its
#             .deps sidecar names, typechecked as one project)?
#   codes     the sorted, deduped set of LB diagnostic codes `luabox check
#             --format json` reports for that file set — empty for a clean
#             row, spelled `-`. Asserted exactly, not just "diag" — "not
#             clean" alone can't distinguish an intended code from an
#   note      REQUIRED on every row (there is no divergence axis here to
#             gate it on) — what regression shape this row pins. An empty
#             note is refused by the script, not just discouraged.
# Every row below was MEASURED against the shipped binary at the time it was
# expected.tsv" for how to re-derive these against a chosen baseline. This
# is a self-regression oracle, not a parity oracle: there is no second tool
# to agree or disagree with, only "does this still say what it used to say".

column4: note
control: a trivial well-typed call has nothing to report; proves the harness itself runs a case end to end

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md: two UNRELATED parents (`: IdxP1, IdxP2`) each declaring the same indexer key is first-listed-wins. IdxP1 (number) is listed first, so `c.anything` types as number: the fixture's ONE call, `want_number(c.anything)`, is clean under the correct order. Verified by construction: swapping to `IdxChild : IdxP2, IdxP1` makes IdxP2 (string) the winner and measures LB0300 ("expected number, found string") on this same call — a first-vs-last flip now changes this row's verdict outright (clean to diag) instead of merely moving an LB0300 from one line to another

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md: one ancestor (DiaBase<T>) reached TWICE through a generic diamond with different type arguments (DiaMid1: DiaBase<number>, DiaMid2: DiaBase<string>) is last-listed-wins — the opposite rule from the unrelated-parents case above. DiaLeaf lists DiaMid2 last, so `c.anything` types as string: the fixture's ONE call, `want_string(c.anything)`, is clean under the correct order. This is the exact rule an intermediate build of this release collapsed into a single last-wins rule for BOTH shapes, silently changing verdicts in both directions (limitations.md, "measured against the pre-change binary rather than derived"). Verified by construction: swapping to `DiaLeaf : DiaMid2, DiaMid1` makes DiaMid1 (number) the winner and measures LB0300 ("expected string, found number") on this same call — this row and the one above are that measurement, committed, now as a clean-vs-diag flip rather than a same-code-either-way tie

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md: two declarations of a generic class spelling the parameter differently (BoxedT<T>/BoxedT<U>) unify their type parameters POSITIONALLY when merged, so slot 0 is one type variable however each declaration spells it. `BoxedT<string>` makes both `value` (declared via T) and `other` (declared via U) read as string — both `want_string` calls are clean, proving the cross-declaration unification actually happened rather than leaving `other` unknown — and the `want_number(b.value)` call is the LB0300 that proves `value` is concretely `string`, not lenient

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, INDEXER table, dup-same-file: a same-key `---@field [K] V` re-declared on ONE class name (two `---@class IdxSame` blocks) is first-wins, the same deterministic rule a duplicate named `---@field` follows -- and, since round 6 review M11, WITH the same LB0311 warning. This row read `clean` until M11 and that silence WAS the finding: the resolution had already been unified onto the named field's rule (`indexer_resolution` derives from `member_wins`) while the diagnostic had not, so one rule ran on two mechanisms and a conflicting indexer resolved with no signal while the identical conflict on a named field warned. Measured against the oracle before the row was moved: lua-language-server 3.13.5 reports `duplicate-doc-field  Duplicate defined fields `[string]`.` on this exact fixture, so this is luals parity, not luabox inventing strictness. The codes column is what pins it -- a bare diag/clean flip cannot tell LB0311 from an unrelated LB0300, and the sibling row field_dup_same_file_first_wins asserts the same code set for the named half, so the two kinds can no longer drift apart without one of the two rows failing.

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md: type parameters are scoped to the declaration that writes them — a declaration naming ANOTHER declaration's parameter is a genuine unknown type name. ScopedT<T>'s own `mistaken` field is annotated `U`, which only ScopedT<U>'s (separate) declaration defines; U is out of scope for the first block and is reported LB0305 ("unknown type name `U`") at the point it's used, not silently treated as the other declaration's T

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md: the parameter LIST follows the same first-wins rule as every other member, so a duplicate declaring MORE parameters than the first (SurplusT<T> then SurplusT<T, V>) has no canonical slot for the surplus — `extra` (declared via the second declaration's V) has no slot to substitute into and stays `unknown` rather than becoming a placeholder no instantiation could satisfy. MEASURED (not the naive assumption): passing that `unknown`-typed value to a `number` parameter under `[types] strict = true` is itself flagged LB0300 ("found unknown") — the leniency is in what `extra` is DECLARED as, not a blanket pass on every later use of it; `want_string(b.value)` stays clean, confirming `value` (T, bound to string) is unaffected by the surplus slot

docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md, "The `__index`-less carrier: member resolution falls through": `setmetatable({}, FallCounter)` with no `FallCounter.__index = FallCounter` still resolves `c:value()` as if `__index` were set (luals parity; #33) — the doc's own worked example, verbatim — so `print(c:value())` produces NOTHING. The fall-through is scoped, not a blanket "anything goes" on the carrier: `c:nonexistent()` in the same file still reports LB0306, which is the ONE diagnostic this row's codes column pins — a regression that either (a) starts flagging `value()` too, or (b) stops flagging `nonexistent()`, both change this row

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, dup-same-file: two `---@class Foo` blocks in one file each declaring `x` (number then string) is first-declaration-wins, the same rule duplicate_indexer_same_class_first_wins pins for indexers, and since round 6 review M11 with the same LB0311 duplicate-field warning the indexer case used to omit -- the codes column pins that emission too. First declaration (number) wins, so `want_string(f.x)` is the LB0300

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, dup-cross-file: a.lua declares x as number, b.lua as string, both `---@class Foo`; first-PROCESSED-file wins -- measured both as-declared and reversed in the scratch report, confirming genuine file-order dependence rather than a value-based tie-break. a.lua is processed first here, so `want_string(f.x)` is the LB0300 that pins it

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, unrelated-parents: `C : P1, P2` with P1.x=number, P2.x=string is FIRST-listed-parent-wins for a plain field (production-readiness-assessment-9natxz A1, finding 6) -- MOVED from clean to diag by this fix. Previously last-listed-parent-wins (the opposite of indexer/operator/visibility's first-listed rule for the identical shape), defended in docs/03-reference/02-limitations.md as an intentional asymmetry; measured against lua-language-server 3.13.5's own source and found backwards -- luals resolves first-listed uniformly (compiler.lua:369-375/424, confirmed by swapping parent order in the pinned binary and watching the enforced type flip). P1 is now listed first and wins, so c.x is number: `want_string(c.x)` is LB0300 ("expected string, found number") where it used to be clean. Verified by construction: swapping to `C : P2, P1` makes P2 (string) the first-listed winner and measures the same call CLEAN instead -- pinned as field/unrelated-parents's `C:P2,P1` variant in class_merge_precedence_matrix.rs -- the same single-call discipline indexer_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins and operator_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins already use for their identical shapes, and now field agrees with both instead of being the one exception

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, diamond-identical: Base<V> reached twice via A:Base<number>, B:Base<number> (both edges agree -- nothing to arbitrate) still has to actually SUBSTITUTE the parameter; item resolves to number, so `want_string(c.item)` is LB0300 'expected string, found number'. The pre-refactor `develop` binary leaked the raw type-parameter name `V` into this same LB0300 instead of resolving it (a declared CHANGELOG fix) -- codes alone cannot distinguish 'resolved to number' from 'leaked as V' (both are LB0300), so this row only catches a total loss of substitution (the diagnostic disappearing or naming a different code), not a regression back to the V-leak specifically

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, diamond-conflicting: Base<V> reached twice via A:Base<number>, B:Base<string> (genuinely conflicting) is LAST-visited-ancestry-edge-wins, confirmed both directions in the scratch measurement. B (string) is visited last, so item is string: `want_string(c.item)` is clean. Field counterpart to indexer_diamond_last_listed_wins and, since finding 3's fix, operator_diamond_conflicting_last_visited_wins too -- all three member kinds now agree on last-visited-edge-wins for the identical diamond-conflicting shape (previously operators were the one first-visited outlier, finding 3 in the scratch report, now fixed)

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, FIELD table, bound-vs-bare: SubBound : Base<number> binds the parent's type parameter correctly (`want_string(sd.item)` reports 'expected string, found number' -- the declared fix over `develop`, which never bound it at all); SubBare : Base (no args) leaves the parameter free and leaks its literal name `T` into `want_string(sb.item)`'s diagnostic instead ('expected string, found T') -- documented as 'stays free' in limitations.md, but the literal-name spelling itself is not promised anywhere (finding 5). Both diagnostics are LB0300, so this row's codes column collapses to one entry; it pins that BOTH halves keep erroring at all, not the concrete `number` vs `T` distinction within that single code

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, METHOD table, dup-same-file: a class carried more than once in one file (F1:m() returns 1, F2:m() returns "s", both annotated ---@class Foo) resolves f:m() to F1's -- the FIRST-declared-in-statement-order carrier's attachment. `want_string(f:m())` is LB0300 'expected string, found 1', proving F1's return type won, not F2's string

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, METHOD table, declaration-vs-attachment: a `---@field m fun(): string` declaration alongside a same-named carrier attachment `function F.m() return 1 end` resolves to the FIELD declaration's type, discarding the attachment's own inferred type -- `want_string(F.m())` is clean. A regression that let the attachment's inferred `number` return win instead would make this LB0300

Finding 1 (FIXED) behind docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md: same-file inheritance of a carrier-attached method through `: Parent` used to not resolve AT ALL -- P1's carrier attaches `function T1:m()` in the SAME file as `---@class C : P1`, and `c.m` reported LB0306 'undefined field m on C' even though m visibly exists on P1. Root cause: the CLI batch path folds every project file's surface, itself included, into the ambient before checking any file, so `env.classes["P1"].methods` WAS seeded correctly -- but `absorb_block`'s handling of a first-time local `---@class` declaration overwrote the seeded `ClassDef` wholesale, discarding that `methods` map, and nothing else in `absorb_block` ever repopulated it before this file's own obligations were checked. `absorb_block` now carries a pre-existing entry's `methods` forward across that overwrite. `c.m` now resolves cleanly, matching method_cross_file_inheritance_control's already-clean verdict for the identical shape -- a regression back to LB0306 here (with method_cross_file_inheritance_control staying clean) would mean same-file inheritance broke again while cross-file stayed fine, the exact asymmetry this pair exists to catch

Finding 1's contrast case: the IDENTICAL inheritance shape as method_same_file_inheritance_gap (P1 attaches `function T1:m()`, `C : P1` reads `c.m`), but P1 now lives in its own file (p1.lua) -- `c.m` resolves cleanly, because merge_file_types folds the already-collected `.methods` map across files. Now matches method_same_file_inheritance_gap's verdict too (finding 1 fixed): if this row ever diverges from that one again -- one clean, one LB0306 -- same-file and cross-file inheritance have gone back to disagreeing

Finding 2 (FIXED) behind docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md: a carrier-attached method's signature used to not cross the same-project file boundary AT ALL, even with ZERO duplication -- p1.lua's Foo carries `function F:m() return "s" end` with no `---@class Foo` anywhere else, and `want_number(f:m())` in main.lua used to type `f:m()` as `unknown`, so a call that should error passed silently. Root cause: reifying an unannotated function's return type gates on `InferMode::Check`'s parameter-seeding flag as well as its own -- a flag meant to stop an unannotated PARAMETER guessing from call-site arguments, not to also erase a function's own body-inferred RETURN type. `FileTypes::collect` now trusts a carrier method's inferred return type when folding it into a class's published `methods` surface, so `f:m()` types as `"s"` and `want_number(f:m())` is the LB0300 that pins it -- a regression back to `unknown` here would make this row silently clean again, exactly the false negative finding 2 named

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, INDEXER table, dup-cross-file: a.lua declares `[string] number`, b.lua declares `[string] string`, both `---@class Foo`; first-PROCESSED-file wins, same mechanism as field_dup_cross_file_first_processed_wins. a.lua is processed first, so `want_string(f["k"])` is the LB0300 that pins it

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, INDEXER table, diamond-identical: Base<V>'s indexer reached twice via A:Base<number>, B:Base<number> (agreeing edges) resolves to number -- `want_string(c["k"])` is LB0300 'expected string, found number'. `develop` leaked raw `V` into the identical diagnostic instead (declared fix) -- same codes-cannot-distinguish-the-leak caveat as field_diamond_identical_binding_resolves

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, INDEXER table, bound-vs-bare: same shape and same within-code caveat as field_generic_bound_vs_bare, for the `---@field [K] V` indexer instead of a named field -- SubBound binds the parent's `number` correctly, SubBare leaks the literal `T`; both diagnostics are LB0300

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, OPERATOR table, dup-same-file: two `---@operator add(Foo): R` overloads on one class name (number then string) resolve via the '#114 first-input-that-accepts-the-operand' scan, which picks the first-added signature on this tie -- `want_string(a + b)` is LB0300 'expected string, found number'. Not a duplicate in the field sense (operators dedupe only on exact-signature equality; these are distinct signatures that happen to share an accepted-input type), but the effective winner is still first-declared, same as field/indexer's dup-same-file rows

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, OPERATOR table, dup-cross-file: a.lua/b.lua each declare Foo's `add` overload (number, string); first-processed file's overload wins via the same scan mechanism as operator_dup_same_file_first_wins -- `want_string(a + b)` is LB0300

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, OPERATOR table, unrelated-parents: `C : P1, P2`, each declaring its own `add` overload (P1: number, P2: string), resolves to the FIRST-listed parent (P1) -- matching indexer's first-listed rule for the identical shape but SAME first-listed rule field_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins now pins -- this note previously called the two OPPOSITE, which was true before the luals-parity fix flipped field's unrelated-parents winner from last-listed to first-listed; every member kind agrees on this shape now. The fixture's ONE call, `want_number(a + b)`, is clean under the correct order since P1 (number) wins. Verified by construction: swapping to `C : P2, P1` makes P2 (string) the first-listed winner and measures LB0300 ("expected number, found string") on this same call -- a first-vs-last flip now changes this row's verdict outright (clean to diag) instead of leaving 'an LB0300 fired on one of two calls' either way

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, OPERATOR table, diamond-identical: Base<V>'s `add` operator reached twice via A:Base<number>, B:Base<number> (agreeing edges) resolves `a + b` to number -- `want_string(a + b)` is LB0300. `develop` leaked raw `V` here too (declared fix)

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, OPERATOR table, diamond-conflicting (finding 3, FIXED): operator diamond-conflict now resolves LAST-visited-ancestry-edge-wins -- the IDENTICAL arrival shape (Base<V> reached twice via A:Base<number>, B:Base<string>) that field_diamond_conflicting_last_visited_wins and indexer_diamond_last_listed_wins already resolve this way. Previously operators were the one FIRST-visited outlier (finding 3), an artifact of accumulating overloads as a scanned list ('first whose input accepts the operand', #114) rather than an overwrite-by-key map; `collect_operators` now tags each accumulated overload with its owning ancestor and supersedes that ancestor's earlier entries on a genuinely competing repeat visit, so a diamond-conflicting ancestor only ever leaves the most-recently-visited edge's signature as a scan candidate. B is visited last here, so `a + b` is string: the fixture's ONE call, `want_number(a + b)`, now reports LB0300 ("expected number, found string") where it used to be clean. Verified by construction: swapping to `C : B, A` makes A visited last and measures the same call CLEAN instead -- pinned as operator/diamond-conflicting's `A=string,B=number` variant in class_merge_precedence_matrix.rs, confirming the flip is genuinely order-dependent, not a value-based tie-break

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, TYPE PARAMETER table, dup-same-file (second declaration's list empty): `Boxed<T>` declared first, then a bare `---@class Boxed` (no params) declaring `other: number` second -- the FIRST (non-empty) declaration's parameter list is canonical, matching ClassDef's own doc comment. `want_string(b.value)` on a `Boxed<string>` instance is clean, proving `value` (bound via the first declaration's T) still resolves to string rather than the second, param-less declaration erasing the binding

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, TYPE PARAMETER table, dup-cross-file (differently spelled): the same positional-unification rule generic_positional_unification pins within one file (`Boxed<T>`/`Boxed<U>`), but split across a.lua/b.lua -- slot 0 is one type variable across the file boundary however each file spells it. Both `want_string(b.value)` and `want_string(b.other)` on `Boxed<string>` are clean

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, TYPE PARAMETER table, bound-vs-bare (parent reference): `SubBound : Base<number>` binds the parent's own type-parameter list -- `want_string(sd.item)` is LB0300 'expected string, found number', the declared fix over `develop`, which never applies the parent argument at all and leaks literal `T` instead. Distinct from field_generic_bound_vs_bare/indexer_generic_bound_vs_bare, which pin the FIELD/INDEXER member being substituted through the binding; this row pins the class's own `<T>` parameter-list binding itself

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, VISIBILITY table, dup-same-file (genuinely conflicting: private then protected): the FIRST declaration wins ATOMICALLY with the field itself -- the second `---@field` line is skipped whole, scope included, before its own scope is ever read. Reading `f.x` from outside the class reports LB0311 (duplicate field) plus LB0312 'cannot access private member x of Foo here' -- private (the first declaration's scope) is what's enforced, not protected

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, VISIBILITY table, dup-cross-file (genuinely conflicting): a.lua declares x private, b.lua declares x protected; first-processed file wins, consistent with fields/indexers/operators at this seam -- LB0312 names private (a.lua's scope). Uses the genuinely-conflicting private-vs-protected pair specifically because a private-vs-PUBLIC dup-cross-file pair looks order-independent for the wrong reason (a public field contributes no visibility-map entry at all, so it can never claim the slot regardless of order) -- see the doc's own callout of this exact trap

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, VISIBILITY table, unrelated-parents (finding 4, FIXED): `C : P1, P2` with P1.x private and P2.x PUBLIC (no scope annotation) now resolves to FIRST-listed-parent-wins, matching indexer_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins and operator_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins for the identical 'two unrelated parents' shape. Previously visibility was the one LAST-listed outlier (finding 4), via a third, independent mechanism (`walk_ancestor_names`'s LIFO ancestor stack popping the last-pushed, i.e. last-declared, parent first); the stack now pushes each class's parents reversed, so the pop order matches ordinary first-listed declaration order instead. P1 (private, first-listed) now wins, so reading `c.x` from outside the class reports LB0312 ("cannot access private member x of P1 here") where it used to be clean. Private-vs-public (not private-vs-protected, which denies access either way and hides the direction behind an identical LB0312) makes the winner decide whether LB0312 fires AT ALL. Verified by construction: swapping to `C : P2, P1` makes P2 (public, now first-listed) win and measures the same read CLEAN instead -- pinned as visibility/unrelated-parents's `C:P2,P1` variant in class_merge_precedence_matrix.rs

docs/03-reference/03-class-merge-precedence.md, VISIBILITY table, diamond-identical: `Base` declares private x; `A : Base`, `B : Base`, `C : A, B` -- both diamond edges reach the SAME declaration, so there is nothing to arbitrate (unlike diamond-conflicting, N/A for visibility since scopes are not parameterized by generics). Reading `c.x` reports LB0312 naming Base as owner, confirming the diamond guard does not accidentally break resolution down to an unambiguous single owner

R6 review M34: no METHOD unrelated-parents/diamond row existed even though method is the kind whose verdicts moved most this round, in both directions, WITH a changed diagnostic code (a shape that used to read LB0306 "undefined field" now reads LB0300 "type mismatch" because the method now actually resolves -- a user's `---@diagnostic disable: undefined-field` waiver stops matching, silently, on this exact flip). `MethodChild : MethodP1, MethodP2`, each parent carrying its own `m()` (returns 1 / returns "s"); first-listed MethodP1 wins, so `want_string(c:m())` is LB0300 'expected string, found 1' -- matches class_merge_precedence_matrix.rs's method-D-unrelated-parents cell, measured fresh against the built binary at this head, not copied from the doc. Paired with the swapped variant below to prove genuine order-dependence, the same discipline every other kind's unrelated-parents row in this file already carries

Companion to method_unrelated_parents_first_listed_wins: `MethodChild : MethodP2, MethodP1` (parents reversed) makes MethodP2 ("s") the first-listed winner, so the identical call `want_string(c:m())` is clean instead of LB0300 -- the flip this pair exists to catch is a first-vs-last regression turning this row's verdict itself (clean to diag or back), not merely moving an LB0300 from one line to another

R6 review M34: the method diamond shape had no row either. `MethodBase` declares `m()` returning "s"; `MethodMidA : MethodBase`, `MethodMidB : MethodBase`, `MethodDiamond : MethodMidA, MethodMidB` -- both diamond edges reach the SAME declaration, nothing to arbitrate (matches class_merge_precedence_matrix.rs's method-E-diamond-identical). `want_string(c:m())` is clean, confirming the diamond guard resolves down to the one agreed method rather than erroring or picking `unknown`

R6 review M33: every prior row in this file shared ONE hardcoded manifest (strict = true, flat src/, no defs), so no row could exercise `[types] defs` at all -- the exact axis finding M5 needs (a silently-clean file caused by an ambient class) and this gate could not express. This row ships its own defs_ambient_class_field_type_flows.toml (`[types] defs = ["vdiff_ambient"]`) plus a defs_ambient_class_field_type_flows.defs sidecar naming vdiff_ambient.d.lua, an ambient `---@class VAmbient` `---@field x number`. `want_string(a.x)` on a `---@type VAmbient` local is LB0300 'expected string, found number' -- measured against the built binary; dropping the defs manifest line entirely (control, measured by hand, not committed) makes VAmbient unresolved and the code set becomes LB0305,LB0300 instead, a different set entirely, so the manifest override is genuinely load-bearing for this row's verdict

R6 review M33: the second half of the manifest-override escape hatch -- this row ships field_unbound_generic_lenient_under_strict_false.toml overriding `[types] strict = false`. `VStrictSub : VStrictBase` (no type argument) leaves VStrictBase's `<T>` unbound, so `item` erases to `unknown`; under strict = true (measured by hand, matching field_generic_bound_vs_bare's SubBare half) `want_string(s.item)` is LB0300 'expected string, found unknown', but under strict = false the SAME mismatch is fully suppressed -- not merely downgraded to a warning, absent from the diagnostics array entirely -- so `want_string(s.item)` is clean. Proves the override sidecar is actually read (a driver that silently kept the default strict = true manifest would measure this row as diag, not clean)

R6 review M48: closes the finding that scripts/tests/luals-differential/expected.tsv's generic_carrier_require row (a row outside this task's ownership -- scripts/tests/luals-differential* is not touched here) pins a message-only rendering fix that is structurally invisible at diag/clean + code-set granularity, by its own note's admission, and so "cannot fail" no matter what regresses. This row pins the SAME reify_export mechanism's OTHER half at a granularity this gate's oracle actually has: an UNDECLARED member read off a generic carrier (`---@class VGenericBox<T>` / `---@field item T`) crossing a `require()` boundary with T left unbound is clean here (a template is structural and enforces no member list), where the identical read off a non-generic carrier is LB0306 (measured by hand, not committed -- swap VGenericBox's `<T>` away and `print(b.nope)` becomes LB0306 'undefined field `nope`'). Presence/absence of enforcement is exactly the diag-vs-clean flip this gate's granularity was designed for, unlike the rendering-only fix the excluded row cannot express

#69 (round 6 review M66): the malformed-input axis, which no row in this corpus covered -- every case above assumes `---@class` parses into a well-formed class at all. `---@class : Base` puts the parent list where the name goes, so the header names nothing; every consumer of a `---@class` tag in luabox-types guards on `!c.name.is_empty()`, so this header used to be DROPPED and the file measured `clean` -- silent at the declaration and silent everywhere else, because nothing in the file references the name the class never got. Now LB0320 at the declaration. Measured against lua-language-server 3.13.5 before the code was assigned: `luadoc-miss-class-name` ("<class name> expected") on this exact shape, so this is parity, not luabox inventing strictness. The codes column is what pins it -- a bare clean/diag flip could not tell LB0320 from the LB0305 a consumer would have raised, which is precisely the indirect signal this row exists to replace

#69: the second silent shape. `---@class 123abc` lexes a name token (luacats' `take_name` accepts any run of [A-Za-z0-9_.] so a typo is captured whole and can be quoted back) but `123abc` is not an identifier, so it cannot name a class. This measured `clean` before the fix, the same silence as malformed_class_parents_in_name_slot and for a different reason -- that one has no name, this one has a name that is not usable -- and luals collapses both to the same `luadoc-miss-class-name`, measured against the pinned 3.13.5. Paired with the well-formed controls in crates/luabox-types/tests/malformed_class_headers.rs (`abc123`, `geometry.Point`, `_Private`, `Größe`), which must stay clean: a rule that fired on `contains a digit` rather than on `starts with one` fails there, not here

#69: the one malformed shape that was NEVER silent, and the row that pins what changed about it. `---@class A : P,` names `A` fine; `P` is undeclared and has always reported LB0305 through the ordinary undeclared-parent path, independent of the trailing comma -- an earlier draft of M66 claimed this shape was silent too, and measuring it fresh against the release binary corrected that.
